<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:2, services/fulfillment/k8s/base/service.yaml:2 -->

The service runs as one container of one Deployment, reached through one Service, configured from one
ConfigMap and from a Secret the overlays generate, and patched by two overlays. Everything on this page
is read from those manifests and from the build that produces the image; nothing here is a
recommendation.

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | `fulfillment` |
| Image tag | `latest` |
| Base image | `eclipse-temurin:25-jdk` |
| Container port | `8080` (TCP) |
| Service | `ClusterIP`, port `80` to container port `8080` |
| Replicas | 1 |
| Image pull policy | `IfNotPresent` |
| JVM flags | `-XX:+UseZGC`, `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75` |

: Image, port and service of the deployment. {#tbl-deployment-image}

The image carries the OpenTelemetry agent and a Java runtime. The container filesystem is read-only,
the process runs as a non-root user, privilege escalation is disabled, all capabilities are dropped,
and an empty `tmp` volume is the only writable path. The base manifest declares those settings and
both overlays repeat them.

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:24, services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:87, services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/dev/deployment-patch.yaml:16, services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/dev/deployment-patch.yaml:30, services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:15 -->

| Resource | Request | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `250m` | `1` |
| `memory` | `768Mi` | `1.5Gi` |

: Resource requests and limits of the base container. {#tbl-deployment-resources}

The `dev` overlay asks for less than the base and caps the container lower as well; the `k3d` overlay
declares no resources of its own and therefore leaves the base values in place.

### 2.1 Environment variables and where they come from

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:24, services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:87 -->

Six environment variables are declared on the container. Three hold connection details and are read
from one Secret, two are read from the ConfigMap, and the profile is written as a literal.

| Variable | Source | Name | Key or value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | literal | — | `prod` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` | Secret | `fulfillment-db` | key `jdbc-url` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` | Secret | `fulfillment-db` | key `username` |
| `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | Secret | `fulfillment-db` | key `password` |
| `SPRING_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` | ConfigMap | `fulfillment` | key `kafka-bootstrap-servers` |
| `JWT_ISSUER_URI` | ConfigMap | `fulfillment` | key `JWT_ISSUER_URI` |

: Environment variables of the container, with the object each one is read from. {#tbl-deployment-environment}

The base ConfigMap declares the keys `kafka-bootstrap-servers`, `spring-profile-active`; the container additionally
reads `JWT_ISSUER_URI` from that ConfigMap. The base declares no such key, and the `dev` overlay does
not add one, so that reference resolves only under the `k3d` overlay, which supplies the key. GAP-2
records what follows from that.
<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/configmap.yaml:8, services/fulfillment/k8s/base/configmap.yaml:9 -->

### 2.2 Probes

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:73, services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:80 -->

| Probe | Declared by | Path | Port | Initial delay | Period | Timeout | Failure threshold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `livenessProbe` | base | `/actuator/health/liveness` | 8080 | 30 | 10 | 5 | — |
| `readinessProbe` | base | `/actuator/health/readiness` | 8080 | 20 | 5 | 3 | — |
| `startupProbe` | `k3d` overlay | `/actuator/health/liveness` | 8080 | 10 | 10 | — | 60 |

: Probes that keep the container alive and route traffic to it. {#tbl-deployment-probes}

Neither base probe declares a failure threshold, so the platform default applies: three consecutive
failures before the container is restarted or taken out of the Service. The `k3d` overlay adds a
startup probe on the liveness path with a threshold of sixty attempts, which at its ten-second period
gives a cold start ten minutes before the liveness probe takes over.

### 2.3 Profiles and overlays

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:46, services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:30 -->

| Profile | Activated in |
|---|---|
| `prod` | the base manifest, as a literal |
| `dev` | the `k3d` overlay |

: Spring profiles the manifests activate. {#tbl-deployment-profiles}

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/dev/kustomization.yaml:2, services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/k3d/kustomization.yaml:2 -->

| Overlay | Namespace | Name prefix | Pull policy | Requests | Limits | ConfigMap keys | Secret keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` | `fulfillment-dev` | `dev-` | `Always` | cpu 100m, memory 256Mi | cpu 500m, memory 512Mi | `kafka-bootstrap-servers`, `spring-profile-active` | `jdbc-url`, `password`, `username` |
| `k3d` | `fulfillment` | none | `IfNotPresent` | — | — | `kafka-bootstrap-servers`, `spring-profile-active`, `JWT_ISSUER_URI` | `jdbc-url`, `password`, `username` |

: Overlays, the namespace they deploy into and what each one patches. {#tbl-deployment-overlays}

The `dev` overlay deploys into its own namespace under a `dev-` name prefix and points the datasource
at a database on the local machine. The `k3d` overlay keeps the shared namespace, adds an Ingress,
generates the secret inline, and is the only overlay that declares the telemetry settings and the
issuer address.

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/overlays/k3d/deployment-patch.yaml:15 -->

| Variable | Source | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` | literal | `dev` |
| `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` | literal | `-javaagent:/app/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar` |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | literal | `fulfillment` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | literal | `http://otel-collector:4317` |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | literal | `grpc` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` | literal | `otlp` |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` | literal | `otlp` |
| `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` | literal | `none` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` | literal | `parentbased_traceidratio` |
| `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` | literal | `1.0` |

: Environment variables the `k3d` overlay adds. {#tbl-deployment-overlay-environment}

### 2.4 Manifests the facts come from

| Manifest | Declares |
|---|---|
| `deployment.yaml` | the Deployment: replicas, container, environment, probes, resources, pod security |
| `service.yaml` | the ClusterIP Service on port 80 |
| `configmap.yaml` | the ConfigMap the container reads two variables from |
| `deployment-patch.yaml`, `dev` overlay | the patch applied to the Deployment |
| `kustomization.yaml`, `dev` overlay | the kustomization that composes the overlay |
| `deployment-patch.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the patch applied to the Deployment |
| `ingress.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the Ingress in front of the Service |
| `kustomization.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the kustomization that composes the overlay |
| `namespace.yaml`, `k3d` overlay | the Namespace the overlay deploys into |

### 2.5 Infrastructure the service depends on

<!-- evidence: services/fulfillment/k8s/infra/kafka.yaml:2, services/fulfillment/k8s/infra/keycloak.yaml:2, services/fulfillment/k8s/infra/otel-collector.yaml:2 -->

Three manifests describe the objects the service uses and no overlay composes them: the broker, the
token issuer with the realm it imports, and the collector that receives the telemetry. They are
applied separately from the application overlay, so an overlay applied on its own brings up a service
whose dependencies are assumed rather than deployed.

| Manifest | Objects it declares |
|---|---|
| `kafka.yaml` | `Service fulfillment-kafka`, `Deployment kafka` |
| `keycloak.yaml` | `ConfigMap keycloak-realm`, `Service fulfillment-keycloak`, `Deployment keycloak` |
| `otel-collector.yaml` | `ConfigMap otel-collector-config`, `Service otel-collector`, `Deployment otel-collector` |

: Infrastructure manifests outside the application kustomization. {#tbl-deployment-infrastructure}
